android.desc:
FBReader — a fast, lightweight, and customizable ebook reader

FBReader opens DRM-free ebooks as well as titles protected with Readium LCP.

Supported ebook formats:
• ePub (including ePub3 features), PDF, Kindle azw3, fb2(.zip)
• Comic books (CBZ/CBR)
• DOC, RTF, HTML, and plain text

Great for language learners:
• Instant word and phrase lookups through your preferred dictionary app

Cloud sync (optional):
• Sync your library and reading positions using the FBReader Book Network, a Google Drive based service
• Disabled by default; enable it in Settings

Highly customizable:
• Use your own TrueType/OpenType fonts and custom backgrounds
• Day and night color themes
• Adjust brightness with a simple swipe along the screen edge
• Fine-tune layout, gestures, and appearance

Optimized for every screen:
• Works smoothly on phones and tablets
• Fully optimized for e-ink devices while still performing excellently on standard LCD and AMOLED screens

Easy access to books:
• Built-in browser for online catalogs and OPDS stores
• Support for custom OPDS catalogs
• Or place ebooks directly in your device’s Books folder

Made for readers worldwide:
• Localized in 34 languages
• Includes hyphenation patterns for 24 languages

quotes.text:
> The OPDS feed is mainly for reading systems and libraries, not for human consumption.

Understood. I was using a standard RSS reader to parse the feed.

I added the OPDS feed to my FBReader app on Android [0] via its Network Catalog feature [1]. Et voila, I have your entire catalog at my fingertips. Thanks. :-)

> It's all volunteer-based so if you're interested in contributing work somehow then drop me a line.

I can definitely see myself volunteering. Thanks for the invite. :-)

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.geometerplus.zlibrary.ui.android

[1] https://fbreader.org/content/documentation/own-opds
